report:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Moderate degenerative subchondral cystic changes are present at the trochlea, lateral greater than medial. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. Mild, diffuse synovial proliferation. No loose intra-articular bodies are seen. Small, ruptured Baker cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: There is a horizontal tear along the posterior horn extending to the root attachment. Mild extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Cartilage appears intact.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: There is tearing of the inner margin along the body and posterior horn. No extrusion.
Lateral compartment cartilage: There is full-thickness cartilage fissuring at the posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: There is mild to moderate cartilage thinning and fissuring at the patella diffusely. Severe cartilage loss is present at the trochlea diffusely with subchondral cystic changes.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild tendinosis.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 10 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:


1. Medial and lateral meniscal tear.

2. Tricompartmental chondrosis, most prominent at the trochlea.

3. Mild quadriceps tendinosis.

4. Moderate joint effusion with synovial proliferation. Small, ruptured Baker cyst.

MRI LEFT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
Severe edema of the medial condyle of left knee.

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
Prior MRI dated <[Date]> of <[Month]> <[YEAR]>

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: Nonsurfacing hyperintensity of the posterior horn probably represents intra since degeneration. No definite meniscal tear. No para meniscal cyst.

Medial meniscus: Oblique tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with extension to the inferior articular surface. Findings are ready seen on prior study but appears more degenerate. Several para meniscal cysts are seen at the posterior aspect of the meniscus measuring up to 0.4 cm in size. Meniscal extrusion approximately 0.6 cm noted.

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: intact

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is normally positioned within the femoral groove. There is no retinacular disruption.

Fluid

No joint effusion or loose body. Trace Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: A large subchondral cysts are seen at the posterior superior aspect of the tibial plateau, very much larger than prior study. Moderate degenerative changes multiple osteophytes are seen, most significant at the medial tibiofemoral joint. No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Minimal chondrosis..

Medial compartment: Focal full-thickness chondral loss measuring up to 1.3 cm in size associated subchondral edema. Moderate chondrosis in the rest of the femoral condyle Findings have slightly progressed compared to prior study.

Lateral compartment: Mild chondral irregularity. No significant subchondral edema.

Others:

Hoffas fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT
Oblique tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with extension to the inferior articular surface, similar to previous. Interval increase in degenerative changes of the meniscus is observed. Meniscal extrusion of approximately 0.6 cm is seen. Multiple para meniscal cysts are also present.

Interval increase in degenerative changes are identified evident as shown by increased osteophytes, full-thickness chondral loss at the medial tibiofemoral joint associated increasing subchondral edema, and multiple enlarging subchondral cysts at the posterior medial tibial plateau.

In the medial compartment, the meniscus is not torn. There is focal high grade chondral defect at mid weight-baring medial femoral condyle (about intact8*1.4 cm).  
 The lateral compartment, appears normal including meniscus and articular cartilage.  
 The patellofemoral joint, there is focal high grade chondral defect (more than 50% thickness cartilage loss) at medial trochlea (about 1*2 cm). The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
 The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact. There is no tibial translation. 
 The medial and lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact. The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact. The meniscopopliteal fascicles are intact. The popliteofibular ligament is intact. 
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 Large amount of left knee effusion with synovitis is present. There is a 5*4*6.5 cm baker's cyst at the posteromedial aspect of left knee. The surrounding musculature is normal. There is no fracture or bone contusion.  -- Focal high grade chondral defect at mid weight-baring medial femoral condyle (about intact8*1.4 cm) and medial trochlea (about 1*2 cm). 
 -- Large amount of left knee effusion with synovitis. 
 -- A 5*4*6.5 cm baker's cyst at the posteromedial aspect of left knee.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left medial knee pain after tripping and striking left knee on a box at work.  History of RA. 
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.  

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES: 
Marked marrow edema in the lateral tibial plateau. Alignment is anatomic.  No aggressive osseous lesions.  

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst. 

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Radial oblique tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with mild extrusion. 6 x 3 mm parameniscal cyst at the posterior horn, body junction. 
Medial compartment cartilage: Diffuse high-grade cartilage loss, weightbearing portion of the femoral condyle. 8 x 5 mm full-thickness cartilage defect posterior weightbearing portion of the femoral condyle. High grade partial thickness cartilage loss of the tibial plateau. 

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.  
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade cartilage fraying spanning the lateral compartment. 

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT: 
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Mild heterogeneity of the patellar cartilage.     

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.  
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.  

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal. 
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.  
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal. 

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear. 
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear. 
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.  
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad.  No lateral patellar tilt or translation.  No patella alta.  Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm. 

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy.  Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact. 

SOFT TISSUES:
Edema identified in the medial subcutaneous fat. 
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. 

IMPRESSION:
1.	Intense marrow edema in the medial tibial plateau. Findings may reflect contusion or severe osseous stress response/developing stress fracture.
2.	Radial oblique tear of the medial meniscus with mild extrusion.
3.	High-grade medial compartment chondrosis.

Small suprapatellar effusion, a cluster of variably sized ossific loose bodies is appreciated posteromedially, the largest on measuring just over 1 cm across.

The medial meniscus appears intact.  
There is incomplete, chronic looking loss of lateral meniscal tissue throughout the corresponding posterior half, together with diffuse full-thickness chondral loss affecting the lateral tibial plateau.
No displaced meniscal fragments are present. 

Focal grade 3 chondral loss noted at the medial retropatellar facets, relatively mild age-related thinning of medial weightbearing hyaline cartilage.
There are nonetheless medial and lateral femorotibial marginal osteophytes.
Intact cruciate and collateral ligaments, popliteus musculotendinous unit, distal iliotibial band and the patellar tendon.
Chronic looking calcific, quiescent distal insertional quadriceps tendinosis.
No fracture or marrow infiltration.
Grossly unremarkable imaged extra-articular soft tissues.
